_comment: PL-22 — does the pilot's 93% hold OUTSIDE the four modules it measured? The original eight were a deterministic stride across source files with a matching test, plus envMerge.ts as a CONTROL: if the harness stops reproducing its known score, none of the other numbers mean anything. WIDENED 2026-08-31 with FOUR UI-layer modules (hooks, helpers, view-models under ui/) by the same stride method. Before that the sample was 8 modules with nothing from the UI layer at all, so the weighted score described the service half and was reported as the number for the whole codebase. COMPONENTS (.tsx) ARE STILL NOT MEASURED, and it is a tooling conflict rather than a choice — see the backlog item on component mutation coverage. Two blockers: 41 of 203 component suites carry a @jest-environment pragma that Stryker cannot read coverage through, and removing it breaks them under Stryker's SANDBOX where the jest project config no longer applies; separately, 33 suites use user-event, whose clipboard teardown throws in Stryker's jsdom environment. The original eight are KEPT AND UNCHANGED so their pinned baselines stay comparable.
